title: His lying face
setting: A weekday evening. Yuki's mother leaves her a voicemail about Kenji, who has been coming home late all week.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? okaasan da kedo. kenji, konshuu zutto kaeri ga osoi no.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。ケンジ、今週ずっと帰りが遅いの。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。けんじ、こんしゅうずっとかえりがおそいの。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? It's Mum. Kenji's been coming home late all week.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: tomodachi to benkyou shiteru tte iu kedo, are wa uso tsuiteru kao yo.
lines.ja: 友達と勉強してるって言うけど、あれは嘘ついてる顔よ。
lines.kana: ともだちとべんきょうしてるっていうけど、あれはうそついてるかおよ。
lines.english: He says he's studying with friends, but I know that face. He's lying.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kinou mo juuichiji made kaette konakatta kara, monku itta no.
lines.ja: 昨日も十一時まで帰ってこなかったから、文句言ったの。
lines.kana: きのうもじゅういちじまでかえってこなかったから、もんくいったの。
lines.english: Yesterday he didn't get in till eleven again, so I complained to him about it.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou shitara, monku bakkari iwanaide yo. boku mo shigoto ga isogashii n da kara tte.
lines.ja: そうしたら、「文句ばっかり言わないでよ。僕も仕事が忙しいんだから」って。
lines.kana: そうしたら、「もんくばっかりいわないでよ。ぼくもしごとがいそがしいんだから」って。
lines.english: And he goes, "Stop complaining all the time. I'm busy with work too, you know."

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shigoto tte nani yo. mou, sonna joudan itte.
lines.ja: 仕事って何よ。もう、そんな冗談言って。
lines.kana: しごとってなによ。もう、そんなじょうだんいって。
lines.english: Work? What work? Honestly, cracking jokes like that.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: gomen ne, guchi bakkari itte. kenji ni monku itte mo, kiite kurenai kara.
lines.ja: ごめんね、愚痴ばっかり言って。ケンジに文句言っても、聞いてくれないから。
lines.kana: ごめんね、ぐちばっかりいって。けんじにもんくいっても、きいてくれないから。
lines.english: Sorry, all I'm doing is moaning. Complaining to Kenji gets me nowhere. He doesn't listen.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, kesa satou-san ni mo guchi ittara ne, kenji, keeki no omise de baito shiteru n datte!
lines.ja: で、今朝佐藤さんにも愚痴言ったらね、ケンジ、ケーキのお店でバイトしてるんだって！
lines.kana: で、けささとうさんにもぐちいったらね、けんじ、けーきのおみせでばいとしてるんだって！
lines.english: So this morning I was moaning to Satou-san too, and he says Kenji's got a part-time job at a cake shop!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: raishuu, okaasan no tanjoubi desho? dakara uso tsuiteta no ne.
lines.ja: 来週、お母さんの誕生日でしょ？だから嘘ついてたのね。
lines.kana: らいしゅう、おかあさんのたんじょうびでしょ？だからうそついてたのね。
lines.english: It's my birthday next week, isn't it? So that's why he was lying.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shigoto ga isogashii tte, joudan itteta n ja nakatta no ne.
lines.ja: 仕事が忙しいって、冗談言ってたんじゃなかったのね。
lines.kana: しごとがいそがしいって、じょうだんいってたんじゃなかったのね。
lines.english: And all that about being busy with work. He wasn't joking after all.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki mo shitteta n desho? zutto okaasan ni naisho ni shiteta no ne.
lines.ja: ユキも知ってたんでしょ？ずっとお母さんに内緒にしてたのね。
lines.kana: ゆきもしってたんでしょ？ずっとおかあさんにないしょにしてたのね。
lines.english: You knew too, didn't you? You've been keeping it from me all this time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kono hanashi, kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne. raishuu wa, bikkuri shita kao suru kara.
lines.ja: この話、ケンジには内緒にしてね。来週は、びっくりした顔するから。
lines.kana: このはなし、けんじにはないしょにしてね。らいしゅうは、びっくりしたかおするから。
lines.english: Don't say a word of this to Kenji, okay? Next week I'll put on my surprised face.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okaasan mo uso tsuku no, jouzu ja nai kedo ne. jaa ne.
lines.ja: お母さんも嘘つくの、上手じゃないけどね。じゃあね。
lines.kana: おかあさんもうそつくの、じょうずじゃないけどね。じゃあね。
lines.english: Mind you, I'm not much good at lying either. Bye!

questions.english: What does Okaasan find out, and what is she going to do?
questions.ja: お母さんは何がわかりましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなにがわかりましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nani ga wakarimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji has been out at karaoke with his friends, and she wants Yuki to have a word with him.
Kenji's late nights are a part-time job at a cake shop, because her birthday is coming, and she'll pretend she doesn't know.
Kenji really has been studying with friends, and she feels bad for complaining at him.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenji has been late all week and says he's studying with friends, but Okaasan is sure he's lying (uso tsuiteru kao). Line 7: Satou-san tells her Kenji has a part-time job at a cake shop. Line 8: her birthday is next week, so that's why he lied (dakara uso tsuiteta no ne). Line 11: she asks Yuki not to tell Kenji (kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne) and says she'll put on a surprised face. A is wrong: karaoke never comes up, and far from asking Yuki to talk to Kenji, she asks her to say nothing. C is wrong: he wasn't studying, he was working (line 7), and her only apology is to Yuki, for moaning (line 6: gomen ne, guchi bakkari itte).

questions.english: You've told Kenta you've started getting up at five every morning. He doesn't buy it: "e, mainichi goji ni okiteru no? uso desho?" (Wait, you're up at five every day? You're kidding, right?) Tell him you're not lying.
questions.ja: え、毎日五時に起きてるの？嘘でしょ？
questions.kana: え、まいにちごじにおきてるの？うそでしょ？
questions.romaji: e, mainichi goji ni okiteru no? uso desho?
questions.answer: Deny it with uso o tsuku in the negative -teru form: honto da yo. uso tsuitenai yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto da yo. uso tsuitenai yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとだよ。嘘ついてないよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: uso tsuitenai tte! honto ni goji ni okiteru n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 嘘ついてないって！ほんとに五時に起きてるんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not lying, I swear! I really do get up at five.

questions.explanation: Lying takes tsuku: uso o tsuku, here as uso tsuitenai (I'm not lying), with o dropped as usual in casual speech. Okaasan uses the same verb in line 2 (uso tsuiteru kao), line 8 (uso tsuiteta) and line 12 (uso tsuku no). English 'tell a lie' points to iu, and natives do say uso bakkari itte, but the set phrase for lying is tsuku. Kenta's uso desho? on its own just means 'you're kidding, right?', so the verb has to come from you. To someone like Satou-san you'd say uso wa tsuitemasen.

questions.english: Okaasan says, "shigoto ga isogashii tte, joudan itteta n ja nakatta no ne." What has she realised?
questions.ja: ケンジの「仕事が忙しい」は、どういうことでしたか？
questions.kana: けんじの「しごとがいそがしい」は、どういうことでしたか？
questions.romaji: kenji no shigoto ga isogashii wa, dou iu koto deshita ka?

choices.english: Kenji was teasing her, because she's the one who's always busy.
Kenji has stopped joking around and started taking his studies seriously.
Kenji wasn't joking when he said he was busy with work: he really does have a job.

questions.explanation: Line 9: joudan itteta n ja nakatta = he wasn't joking. In line 4 Kenji said boku mo shigoto ga isogashii n da kara, and in line 5 Okaasan brushed it off as a joke (shigoto tte nani yo. mou, sonna joudan itte). Line 7 shows it was true: he has a part-time job at a cake shop. Jokes are said, with iu (joudan o iu), not made (joudan o tsukuru doesn't work). A is wrong: nobody mentions Okaasan's own work; the 'joke' was a high schooler claiming to be busy with work. B is wrong: he wasn't studying at all (line 7), and the line is about something he said, not about him getting serious.

questions.english: When Okaasan had a go at him for coming home late, what did Kenji say back?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは、お母さんに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんは、おかあさんになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa, okaasan ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Stop doing complaints all the time (monku with suru).
Stop moaning about your lot all the time.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenji answers back with monku bakkari iwanaide yo. A complaint is something you say: monku o iu, here in the -naide form (don't...). Okaasan uses the same pair in line 3 (monku itta no) and line 6 (monku itte mo). B is English 'complain' turned into one verb with suru; Japanese doesn't say monku suru. C has the right verb but the wrong noun for this moment: guchi is moaning to let off steam to someone who'll listen, which is what Okaasan does with Yuki and Satou-san (lines 6-7). What she did to Kenji was object to his face about coming home late, and that is monku.

questions.english: You've spent the whole evening at Kenta's going on about your awful week at work. He looks at the clock: "mou juuniji da yo. kyou wa zutto shigoto no hanashi da ne." (It's midnight already. You've talked about work all night.) Apologise for moaning so much.
questions.ja: もう十二時だよ。今日はずっと仕事の話だね。
questions.kana: もうじゅうにじだよ。きょうはずっとしごとのはなしだね。
questions.romaji: mou juuniji da yo. kyou wa zutto shigoto no hanashi da ne.
questions.answer: Apologise with guchi o iu: gomen, guchi bakkari itte.

modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、愚痴ばっかり言って。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, all I've done is moan.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne, guchi itte. kiite kurete arigatou.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね、愚痴言って。聞いてくれてありがとう。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry for moaning. Thanks for listening.

questions.explanation: guchi o iu is moaning to let off steam, to someone who'll listen, and gomen, guchi bakkari itte is the standard apology afterwards: it's Okaasan's line 6 (gomen ne, guchi bakkari itte). Don't use monku here: monku o iu is objecting to someone or something, the way Okaasan tells Kenji off in line 3. You weren't objecting to Kenta, just letting off steam about your week. Like monku, guchi is said with iu, not suru.

questions.english: You're planning a surprise for Yuki's birthday and you've just told Kenta about it. He asks, "sore, yuki ni mo itte ii?" (Can I tell Yuki too?) Say no, and ask him to keep it from her.
questions.ja: それ、ユキにも言っていい？
questions.kana: それ、ゆきにもいっていい？
questions.romaji: sore, yuki ni mo itte ii?
questions.answer: Say no and ask him to keep it secret with naisho ni suru as a request: dame! yuki ni wa naisho ni shite ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: dame! yuki ni wa naisho ni shite ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ダメ！ユキには内緒にしてね。
modelAnswers.english: No! Keep it from Yuki, okay?

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, kore wa naisho ni shite. onegai.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、これは内緒にして。お願い。
modelAnswers.english: No, keep this between us. Please.

questions.explanation: naisho takes ni suru, and naisho ni shite (ne) is the everyday way to say 'keep this between us', exactly as Okaasan says it in line 11 (kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne). In line 10 she uses it in the past about Yuki (okaasan ni naisho ni shiteta). English 'keep a secret' leads to mamoru, but naisho o mamotte is wrong; mamoru only goes with himitsu (himitsu mamotte ne), and himitsu ni shite works too. The person it's kept from takes ni wa: yuki ni wa.

newWords.english: face; X kao suru = put on an X face (bikkuri shita kao suru = act surprised)
